title: Tell me it is a paid app upfront
body:
I went through the whole process of adding in information and even the cute bear you adopt.

Then it tells me I have 7 days free and then I can pay $50 to keep going.

No one wants to change medical info every 7 days so this really is a paid app not a free one and should be advertised as such.

title: Finally an app that captures everything
body: I’ve been looking for an app for a long time to help me track medications, mood, sleep, menstrual cycle, migraines and more. Bearable allows me to do this and more, and it doesn’t feel like a chore to complete. As someone with ADHD this is super important - I love the little dopamine hits that I get go ticking things off, and it’s easy to use. Love the colours and aesthetics too. I like that I can customise what I need to track and will be able to have easy access to compare factors to help me have a better understanding of what’s going on and to help with medical appointments.

author: pixiehabits

title: Good but room for improvement
body: I would love to see weather metrics available in app as a factor for pain, particularly for trend analysis it’s an important variable. Additionally the statistics being used to determine trends seems somewhat questionable without seeing any of the BTS analyses - but from what I can see a required sample size of 3 for this kind of data seems to only be providing inaccurate results. For example according to my trends I have reduced pain when I 1) have my phone in the bed (this contradicts research), when I am sedentary (this I know makes my pain worse), and when I’m overthinking future events… these are obviously incorrect inferences from correlations of small samples. Since I’m paying so much for premium I expected that the trends at least make sense but now it’s impossible to tease out any true trends without more data. If I had to guess, the model being used isn’t accounting for excess zeros in the data due to people not logging a certain thing, so perhaps the days I was feeling worse were just when I started using the app and so as I started feeling better I added in more detail to the data. But you can adjust for this, and you should be using a ZIP or ZINB model - you shouldn’t be using basic correlation matrices for data this complex. And when it displays results for 2 days vs 1 day - is that dealing with the data collectively or analysing temporal trends? This app is great, and could be amazing if the results are useable.

author: Ginger Globe

title: What a wonderful health champion Bearable is!
body:
I love this app! Using this to track my general health as a very healthy person - but I’m someone who wants to improve my health, my happiness, my productivity and energy levels even more via tracking the effects of all kinds of factors - water, exercises, fresh air, my period, what time I go to bed etc etc. 
It motivates me to do more healthy factors on my list and avoid the ones I suspect make me feel less energetic, happy, productive etc.
I feel so empowered seeing the direct effect each has - as a % gain or loss- to these outcomes! So logical so encouraging, no psychology or mantras - it’s just input and output and great fast analysis. Truly empowering and really simple. Love the bear too - everything is simple and positive about this app.
author: Lana del Kaye

title: Epilepsy management tool
body: Really helpful for epilepsy management with how flexible / editable all the categories are, and with pre-filled seizure, headache, medication options, especially with time period options. Can track triggers well. Great symptom management data tracker in general for anyone who wants to personalise a lot.
author: PamPam992

title: Super helpful app (and developers)
body:
I’ve used bearable for a few years now.
I have three overlapping chronic conditions and balancing treatments for each is difficult - this makes it much easier.
I find just the act of “paying attention” to how I am going each day is so helpful for my mental state; but also being able to look back at the data and find correlations has helped me figure things out that doctors missed.
Also, the developers go above and beyond. I have request feature changes or tweaks more than once, they have communicated with me to clarify what would help, then found a way to work that in without compromising how the app works for other users. An awesome, unheard of, level of customisation.
author: Signor-macaroni

title: So much to love
body:
I really enjoy Bearable! I dropped 1 star as I’d like for the Symptom scores to be more customisable. I’d like to just be able to click “yes” or “no” rather than options 0-4 as my symptoms are pretty consistently the same level. 

While I totally understand the price point and think it’s reasonably priced, unfortunately the cost of the premium features is a blocker for me. I’m on the free trial at the moment and am so sad that I know I won’t be continuing on the paid version as I genuinely can’t afford it long term due to ongoing and unpredictable medical costs ☹️ I’ve entered the Hero raffle, so fingers crossed!! ❤️ I love that this Hero functionality has been built for this app, it’s such an awesome idea and should be a guiding post for similar start ups! 

I really have never been so consistent with a health tracking app before and I really love its features, especially the insights. I’ve finally finished enough days that I can see the trends starting to form in the graphs and can already tell my habit forming is going really well. 

Love you Bearable!

author: omns

title: Most thorough and customisable symptom app out there!
body:
I’ve been managing chronic health conditions for a while and need to track symptoms as I trial new medications. 
I downloaded a bunch of them to play around and find the best one, and as soon as I found this one, I knew it was far superior to the others! It has amazingly in depth pre selection criteria but is also customisable to add your own symptoms, health, or other factors that you’d like to track. Plus it can even send you reminder notifications! I’ve deleted everything else and will just be using this from now on. The only on thing I’d like to see added is a tracker for urination (similar to bowel movements) as my medications can affect my kidneys and bladder. I’ve added it as a few personal notes if I’m going too frequently or can’t empty my bladder fully etc for the time being but hopefully the developers see this review and add it as a feature! :)

title: Exactly what I’ve been looking for!
body:
I’ve tried so many of these apps and none of them have been remotely close to what I wanted. Can’t express how relieved I was to find this one! 

As a scientist (and therefore all too often statistician), I’ve been so curious to analyse the patterns in my environment/behaviour/etc. This app finally allows me to do this and means I don’t have to resort to making one in Excel or R myself. 

As someone who has been (actively!) looking for an app like this for at least five years, you guys have made my day :)
author: msidari

title: Life Changing
body:
This is a must have for the chronically ill and those struggling with mental health. It takes very little effort to fill in each day but the data collected from each individual action, whether it be med change, increased activity, extra therapy appointments etc can all be traced. You get a clear symptom and mood overview. Charts specific to each action. It helps long term planning and increases quality of life. 

The founder used the chronic illness community to develop this app and took feedback the entire time which is a reason why it’s so user friendly and helpful.

With promises for more features in the future, the paid version is well worth the investment.
author: Rachiecandice

title: Worth the money!
body:
This app is highly customisable, and lovely to look at. I can track just about anything, and the amount of insights you can get is amazing.
I see people complaining about the cost. Its still 100% free. If you choose to pay you do get a little extra, but it’s perfectly functional either way. It’s around $5 AUD a month with the yearly subscription. I’m a low income earner and on disability, but I am happy to pay for this to support future development of the app. They even take suggestions for future additions!
